cases.evidence: Numbered tags placed closer than allowed minimum (gap<3).
cases.cause: boundaries generated with insufficient token spacing
cases.proposed_rule: Enforce a minimum source-token gap (e.g. ≥3 tokens) between numbered boundaries; prefer clause- or sentence-level splits when spacing would be violated.

example_pair.input: It was ruled by the "Vichy" French. These were French people who had made peace with the Germans in 1940 and worked with the invaders instead of fighting them.
example_pair.output: It was ruled by the "Vichy" French. <SEG:1> These were French people who had made peace with the Germans in 1940 and worked with the invaders instead of fighting them.

cases.evidence: Piece committed to an agent/possessor ('we') before subordinate clause head; later context assigns agent to 'our ancestors'.
cases.cause: subject/possessive role not yet settled (clause head absent)
cases.proposed_rule: Do not finalize subject/possessive choices or translate pronouns until the clause head and any possessive attachments appear; avoid boundaries that close a subject-verb relation prematurely.

example_pair.input: All things considered, we should not be surprised if our own ancestors solved their "protein problem" in somewhat the same way that chimps on the savanna do today.
example_pair.output: All things considered, <SEG:1> we should not be surprised if our own ancestors solved their "protein problem" in somewhat the same way that chimps on the savanna do today.

cases.evidence: Domain noun 'wicket' was mistranslated (rendered as unrelated sense) because immediate context that disambiguates it was split away.
cases.cause: domain-specific head noun disambiguation needs adjacent context
cases.proposed_rule: Delay translating domain-specific nouns or technical terms until their head and immediate local context (adjacent verbs, numbers, or prepositional phrases) are visible.

example_pair.input: But, after losing the captain's wicket India only made 36 runs loosing 7 wickets to end the innings.
example_pair.output: But, after losing the captain's wicket <SEG:1> India only made 36 runs losing 7 wickets to end the innings.

cases.evidence: Modifiers ('national') were translated before the head noun ('park'), producing 'team'/'national team' errors.
cases.cause: head noun not yet arrived; modifier prematurely attached
cases.proposed_rule: Wait for the head noun before translating modifiers or adjectives that attach to it; avoid boundaries that end a piece inside adjective+head noun sequences.

example_pair.input: The Plitvice Lakes national park is heavily forested, mainly with beech, spruce, and fir trees, and features a mixture of Alpine and Mediterranean vegetation.
example_pair.output: The Plitvice Lakes national park <SEG:1> is heavily forested, mainly with beech, spruce, and fir trees, and features a mixture of Alpine and Mediterranean vegetation.

cases.evidence: Modifier 'long-running' attached to wrong noun because the noun-head ('site'/'radio') was split across pieces; produced 'long-duration Internet site'.
cases.cause: modifier attached before its head noun arrived
cases.proposed_rule: Do not finalize modifier attachment when the head noun is not yet visible; prefer boundaries after the head noun for adjective+head or compound-noun sequences.

example_pair.input: In its early days, the show was featured solely at the long-running internet radio site TogiNet Radio, a site focused on talk radio.
example_pair.output: In its early days, <SEG:1> the show was featured solely at the long-running internet radio site TogiNet Radio, a site focused on talk radio.

cases.evidence: Partial NP was rendered as a completed claim before its complement ('of the seven wonders') arrived, producing an awkward or premature assertion.
cases.cause: NP/complement not complete when boundary closed
cases.proposed_rule: Avoid boundaries that finalize classification/uniqueness claims until complement phrases (e.g., 'of the ...', relative clauses) that qualify them are present.

example_pair.input: The Great Pyramid at Giza is the only one of the seven wonders that is still standing today.
example_pair.output: The Great Pyramid at Giza is the only one of the seven wonders that is still standing today. <SEG:1>

cases.evidence: Numeric quantifier got separated from its clause context; earlier piece produced a predicate about 'percentage' that the later numeric phrase altered, causing contradiction risk.
cases.cause: statistical/quantified noun phrase split from its clause context
cases.proposed_rule: Do not finalize statistical or quantitative claims until the quantified noun phrase and its clause context (e.g., 'of the total ...', attached prepositional phrases) are present.

example_pair.input: However, the percentage of XDR-TB in the entire group of people with tuberculosis still seems to be low; 6,000 of the total 330,000 people infected at any particular moment in South Africa.
example_pair.output: However, the percentage of XDR-TB in the entire group of people with tuberculosis still seems to be low; <SEG:1> 6,000 of the total 330,000 people infected at any particular moment in South Africa.

cases.evidence: Phrasal verb/preposition 'reflect on' was broken by a boundary, producing 'reflect a' and causing mistranslation.
cases.cause: phrasal verb or verb+preposition split across boundary
cases.proposed_rule: Keep phrasal verbs and verb+preposition/object sequences intact; do not end a piece between a verb and its required preposition or immediate object.

example_pair.input: Sharing a field trip virtually is also a great way to reflect on a trip and share experiences with future classes.
example_pair.output: Sharing a field trip virtually is also a great way to reflect on a trip and share experiences with future classes. <SEG:1>

summary: The prompt systematically places high-confidence boundaries inside noun phrases, modifier+head sequences, phrasal verbs, and before numeric or possessive attachments — i.e., it closes pieces before heads/required dependents arrive. It also allows tags that are too close together (format violations). Fixes: forbid boundaries that end a piece before a head noun/verb or required preposition/object, and enforce a minimal token gap between tags.
